items.stem: When does the LINQ query `var q = list.Where(x => x > 0);` actually run its predicate?

options.text: When the query is enumerated, e.g. in a foreach or ToList
options.rationale: Correct: LINQ-to-objects uses deferred execution; the predicate runs on enumeration.

options.text: On the line where q is declared
options.rationale: Declaration does not execute a deferred query.
No compile step is needed for LINQ-to-objects.

options.text: Only if the list is sorted first
options.rationale: Sorting is unrelated to when the predicate runs.

items.explanation: Correct: LINQ-to-objects uses deferred execution; the predicate runs on enumeration.

items.stem: Which TWO are appropriate uses of generic constraints? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Requiring a type parameter to implement an interface so its members can be called
options.rationale: Correct: an interface constraint lets the generic code use those members.

options.text: Requiring a parameterless constructor with new()
options.rationale: Correct: the new() constraint allows constructing T.

options.text: Forcing the JIT to generate separate source files
options.rationale: Constraints do not generate source files.
Constraints do not categorically prevent boxing.

items.explanation: Correct: an interface constraint lets the generic code use those members.

options.text: Cache the reflected metadata instead of re-reading it each call
options.rationale: Correct: reflection is costly; caching results removes repeated metadata lookups.
